header: A used theodolite and an empty shop
lead: Gerhard Tulln bought the theodolite at an auction and rented a former butcher's shop on Bahnhofstraße. The rent was low and the floor was level enough to check instruments on.
bodytext:
Gerhard had worked at the cadastral office in Sandau for eleven years and left the week his second child was born. In the first year he worked alone. The shop had no heating until October 1995, so he drew the plans at the kitchen table.

The office survived its first winter on one contract: four kilometres of the Nauwang sewer, surveyed between January and March. The weather broke two tripods. The municipality paid late and in three parts. Gerhard said the job taught him how to run a business, mostly how to send invoices.

By 2002 there were nine people. By 2010 there were three offices, though that was never the plan. Nauwang and Kettbach each began with one person working from home near the sites. Gerhard handed over to Helene Marchetti in 2016 and still comes in on Thursdays to argue about field books.
caption: Gerhard Tulln, photographed for the 30th anniversary in June 2024.
author: Gerhard Tulln
